results.title: Random slugs can collide and overwrite existing links

triage.reason: Verified in code: createApp calls store.create with a single unchecked slugFn() result, and LinkStore.create overwrites any existing entry at that key, so a fix (loop slugFn() against store.has() until free) is concrete and testable.

work.summary: Fixed POST /links to retry slug generation until an unused slug is found, preventing silent overwrite of existing links on collision. Added a test that forces a collision via injected slugFn and verifies the original link is preserved and a new slug is assigned.

results.title: GET /stats/:slug returns 500 for an unknown slug

triage.reason: Root cause is a missing null-check (non-null assertion `!`) at server.ts:40, same fix pattern as the adjacent redirect route; outcome (404 + specific body) is concretely testable.

work.summary: Fixed GET /stats/:slug returning 500 for unknown slugs. The handler used a non-null assertion (store.get(parts[1])!) on a possibly-undefined result, crashing when accessing link.slug. Now it checks for the missing link and returns 404 {"error": "not found"}, matching the redirect route's behavior. Added a test confirming the 404 response for an unknown slug.

results.title: HEAD requests are counted as clicks

triage.reason: Concrete fix identified: gate store.recordClick on req.method === "GET" in src/server.ts line 47, with testable HEAD vs GET click-count behavior.

work.summary: Fixed HEAD requests to /:slug incrementing the click counter. src/server.ts now only calls store.recordClick when req.method === "GET", while still responding with a 302 and Location header for both GET and HEAD. Added a test verifying HEAD redirects but leaves clicks at 0.

triage.reason: Spec gives exact validation regex, status codes (400/409), and fallback behavior, mapping directly to the existing POST /links handler in src/server.ts.

work.summary: Added custom slug support to POST /links: validates slug against ^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$ (400 if invalid), returns 409 if slug already taken (existing link untouched), and falls back to random slug generation when slug is omitted.

results.title: Links that expire

triage.reason: Specifies a concrete new field, exact status code/body for expired access, and the no-count-on-expiry behavior, all testable against the existing POST /links and GET /:slug handlers in src/server.ts and src/store.ts.

work.summary: Added optional `expiresInSeconds` (positive integer) to POST /links. The link store now records an `expiresAt` timestamp, and GET /:slug checks it: once past expiry, it returns 410 {"error":"expired"} without recording a click; links without the field behave as before. Invalid (non-positive or non-integer) expiresInSeconds returns 400.

triage.reason: Concrete testable outcome specified: new GET /links endpoint with defined response shape, limit/cursor params, and ordering behavior.

work.summary: Added GET /links with cursor pagination: LinkStore.list() returns items sorted by creation order (tie-broken by slug) plus a nextCursor (last item's slug, or null on the final page). The server route parses ?limit= (default 20, capped at 100, invalid values fall back to 20) and ?cursor=, passing them through to store.list(). Added 4 new tests covering ordering, multi-page cursor walking, default/cap limit behavior, and the empty-store case.

issuesFound: src/store.ts: all() now sorts by `createdAt - a.slug.localeCompare(b.slug)` as a tiebreaker. createdAt is millisecond resolution, and slugs are random (src/slug.ts), so when two links are created within the same millisecond (easily happens under concurrent load), GET /links returns them in alphabetical-slug order instead of creation order — violating the issue's 'in creation order' requirement. Previously all() relied on stable sort + Map insertion order to preserve true creation order for ties; this change breaks that guarantee. Reproduced directly: creating links 'zebra, apple, mango, kiwi, banana' at the same timestamp returns them as 'apple, banana, kiwi, mango, zebra'.

test/pagination.test.ts: all tests use a sequentialSlugFn() whose slugs are already monotonically increasing in creation order, so the new slug-based tiebreak in all() is never exercised in a way that could expose the ordering bug — the tests don't actually verify creation-order is preserved independent of slug lexicographic order, and in production (random slugs) the guarantee doesn't hold.

results.title: Rate limit link creation per client

triage.reason: Specifies exact endpoint, limit (10/min per client IP), response code/header, and explicit exclusions, matching the existing no-framework node:http server so it can be implemented and tested directly.

work.summary: Added a per-client-IP rate limiter for POST /links: 10 requests/minute, with the 11th returning 429 and a retry-after header (seconds). Implemented as a small injectable RateLimiter class (src/rateLimiter.ts) wired into createApp via a new optional AppOptions.rateLimiter, keyed by req.socket.remoteAddress. Redirects (GET /:slug) and stats (GET /stats/:slug) are untouched by the limiter. Added test/rateLimit.test.ts covering the 11th-request 429 + retry-after behavior, window reset after retry-after elapses (using an injected fake clock), and confirming redirects/stats remain unlimited.
